changes: WS DM deletion now invalidates pending message work, updates the visible state immediately, and removes the exact 1:1 DM cache row. Matching requires both message ID and DM conversation with an empty server-channel scope; group/server/other-DM rows are not removed.

Cache scope read and deletion share one readwrite IndexedDB transaction. Captured account, composer generation, device and deletion token fence the work before database access, after record lookup and after deletion; context changes before commit abort the transaction.

Duplicate/unloaded deletions no longer guess that an unknown message belongs to a peer and decrement unread counts. Loaded peer deletion still decrements once; repeated delivery does not decrement again. Optional cache cleanup failure is logged without message content.
verification: Targeted storage/WS suites passed: 2 files / 65 tests. Uses real IndexedDB transaction/index behavior through the existing fake-indexeddb harness, including indexed-search removal, scope mismatch preservation, no-op absence, rollback at each guard stage, captured-session invalidation and duplicate deletion unread behavior.
Final TypeScript tsc -b and targeted ESLint passed.

Full client suite passed: 232 files / 2313 tests in 47.58s. Vite production build passed in 706ms with existing warnings. Targeted diff whitespace and coverage validation passed: 33 references / 261 behaviors; acceptance remains incomplete.
remaining: Missed deletion events after offline/reconnect still require authoritative reconciliation. Successful HTTP deletion without its WS event, group/server cache cleanup and cache/search retention policies remain open.

Cache deletion is best effort on storage failure; retry/UI recovery and actual browser/process tests remain required. The existing cache has no per-row account namespace and is not encrypted at rest. This guard is not a claim of complete multi-account or cross-tab cache isolation.
Overall P0-P11 is incomplete. No production data was deleted by this development/test run; no commit, push, merge, Windows packaging or production release performed.
